original_title: Login rate limit keys on req.ip with no trust-proxy config; behind the loopback ingress all users share one bucket
explanation: Trusted Caddy client IP replaces req.ip; separate client and identity keys now exist. Express trust proxy is deliberately disabled.

original_title: Operational queue silently drops older requests: server returns the newest 100 rows regardless of status
explanation: LIMIT 100 precedes client status filtering and counts; older active requests disappear from the UI, but remain in the database and accessible by known ID APIs. This is a functional defect, not an isolation vulnerability.

original_title: No per-account throttling or lockout; limits are in-memory, per-process and per-IP only
explanation: Per-route normalised-identity throttling now blocks distributed guesses against one identity. Memory resets still occur; a shared store is explicitly deferred until a multi-process deployment.

original_title: SECURITY DEFINER functions set search_path without pg_temp
explanation: Missing explicit pg_temp is real in 004/009, but 009 relations are schema-qualified and broker-only. The 004 trigger has an unqualified relation; RLS valid_operating_context separately validates the real binding. A lower-trust SQL path and actual invariant bypass remain unproved.

original_title: Deployed API login role has BYPASSRLS, SELECT on every table and membership of both app roles
explanation: BYPASSRLS and broad reads are explicit trusted development broker capabilities. Request callbacks SET LOCAL ROLE. No supplied path shows an ordinary user bypassing that switch; this does not protect against compromise of the broker itself.

original_title: No Content-Security-Policy, frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options anywhere (app or ingress)
explanation: CSP and framing headers are absent. SameSite Strict cookies constrain authenticated cross-site framing. Missing headers alone do not establish XSS or successful authenticated clickjacking; establish a concrete framed workflow or supported same-site attacker.

original_title: Seed scripts fall back to a public default password with no deployment guard
explanation: Public fallback exists for explicitly local synthetic seeding. Supported F06 bootstrap generates a private random value, and repeat seeds preserve credentials. Current release updates do not reseed. No supported deployment with default credentials was established.

original_title: Runtime database password and credentials handled via aws CLI arguments and a full copy of process.env
explanation: SecretString enters CLI argv during secret creation and children inherit process.env. Actual disclosure requires a lower-trust local process with relevant argv/environment visibility; that actor is not established on the dedicated runtime. Runtime read calls do not pass the retrieved password in argv.

original_title: Authenticated users can trigger three aws CLI spawns inside an open DB transaction per /api/resources/status call
explanation: Current F08 requires resources.read entitlement as well as authenticated non-ADMIN scope, route/context and enabled owned resources. Entitled actors still retain a shared max=10 control-pool client during secret metadata/value retrieval, a new TLS connection and unnecessary STS acquisition. Per-call timeouts exist; no endpoint concurrency/admission budget protects shared capacity. No load or exploit test was performed.

original_title: scrypt is computed synchronously on the event loop for every login and registration
explanation: scryptSync blocks the event loop, and successful council login verifies twice. New client/identity throttling weakens the original combined attack. Distributed identities can still cause work; a meaningful availability impact needs a workload budget or measurement.

original_title: Database pool has no 'error' listener: an idle-connection error crashes the API and both workers
explanation: The exported pg.Pool has no error listener. An emitted unhandled idle-client error can terminate every process using it. systemd restart limits downtime but drops in-flight work. Infrastructure-triggered reliability defect, not an established attacker path.

original_title: Route verification worker handles one route per 10 s but readiness expires after 300 s
explanation: One probe plus ten-second sleep and five-minute expiry remain. Exact capacity depends on probe latency and retries; 25-30 is not guaranteed. Approved runtime has three routes and two councils, so the report does not establish present capacity failure.

original_title: CommandMAPS cannot select an operating context and hard-codes the context label
explanation: Partly superseded by F08: the operational context label now uses entitlement.label or actor.branch_id, and displays actual tenant/jurisdiction. A context chooser remains absent. Ingress still selects the owned context by hostname; local multi-context selection remains a documented limitation. No cross-context authorisation bypass is established.

original_title: Geo assignment silently falls back to a different street's segment and records the number under it
explanation: When no street-name match exists among nearest candidates, pick_best_segment selects a different street. Within-distance addresses are emitted under seg.street without a mismatch flag. Data-quality defect; deployed dispatch consumption is not established.

original_title: Mutating-request origin check allows requests without an Origin header, and the app-level allow-list needs every hostname enumerated
explanation: Ingress enforces canonical same-origin when Origin is supplied; app middleware adds a static allow-list. New hosts need coordinated configuration. Origin-less nonbrowser calls do not by themselves bypass CSRF tokens and Strict cookies. Three approved hosts are configured.

original_title: Test gaps: AWS data-plane code 31% covered, rate limiting untested, no frontend unit tests
explanation: Current source CI includes real Caddy authority/login checks, 429/client/identity cases and three browser suites; F08 release evidence records 75 integration checks. This assessment did not rerun tests, measure coverage or endorse the historical 31% figure. No frontend unit suite or automated cloud acceptance is present in the inspected workflow.

original_title: The platform App component is an 820-line function with four-level nested ternaries
explanation: Platform App remains large with nested views and state. Size indicates review cost, not a demonstrated failure or security boundary violation. Exact old line count is stale.

original_title: Authentication, validation and idempotency helpers are copy-pasted across modules
explanation: Validation, authentication and receipt helpers remain similar across modules, but login throttling is now shared. Intentional council/platform policy differences must survive any extraction; duplication alone is not a defect.

original_title: Client-side path traversal: municipality id from location.hash is used in a fetch path without validation
explanation: readRoute takes only the second slash-delimited hash segment. Literal ../auth does not survive as a complete ID. Encoded dot segments can normalise a GET toward parent/list routes, but server UUID checks and authentication remain; no cross-boundary read or attacker exfiltration is shown.

original_title: Routing probe token compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison
explanation: Probe comparison uses ordinary equality, but remote requests also pass private ingress and loopback checks, and probe returns only route identifiers. A remotely useful timing oracle and meaningful protected consequence are unproved.

original_title: Application role is granted SELECT on the whole users table including password_hash; hashes are loaded into every request object
explanation: Scoped SQL role can read hashes and authentication loads u.*, but actorView whitelists output and officer listing selects explicit columns. No HTTP hash leak exists in the supplied path. Arbitrary SQL under the trusted process is an additional compromise assumption.

original_title: Platform app role can UPDATE every column of provisioning_jobs/provisioning_steps
explanation: Broad job UPDATE grants exist, while actual retry/reconcile APIs restrict legal transitions. The claim requires arbitrary SQL or a compromised broker, already trusted across these councils. Narrower grants would reduce blast radius but no HTTP privilege escalation is demonstrated.

original_title: Predictable temp directory used to stage the esbuild executable
explanation: Predictable temporary directory is not ownership-verified if pre-existing; cross-user precreation is a plausible build-tool attack. Supported lower-trust co-resident users and directory ownership/protections are unknown. A private fresh directory would remove the assumption.

original_title: Local database initialised with trust authentication for the superuser
explanation: Local helper deliberately uses trust on a loopback synthetic database. F06 instead configures SCRAM and rejects other TCP logins. No supported shared-user or public trust-authenticated deployment is established.

original_title: Bootstrap downloads trust anchors from the same origin as the artefact and installs unpinned packages
explanation: Node archive/checksum share a TLS-authenticated origin; a downloaded RDS CA bundle is itself authenticated by HTTPS. These are not unauthenticated downloads. Mutable action tags and package versions are supply-chain hardening opportunities, without a supplied attacker path or compromised artefact.

original_title: Service user owns its own code and units lack further sandboxing
explanation: Ownership does not make /opt writable inside the service mount namespace: ProtectSystem=strict applies and API/routing have no ReadWritePaths exception for source. Claimed normal-process persistent rewrite is defeated by the shipped unit. Root/host compromise is a different boundary.

original_title: Runtime role password is sent in a plain CREATE ROLE ... PASSWORD statement
explanation: Generated CREATE ROLE includes a cleartext password over a certificate-verified TLS connection. Template does not enable statement logging, and password-statement redaction depends on PostgreSQL/logging layer. Secret logging is not established; actual server and audit configuration are needed.

original_title: DDL identifiers are interpolated into SQL strings (validated, but not quoted)
explanation: JS identifiers are fixed prefixes plus validated UUID hex or validated runtime hex. CREATE ROLE already uses server format %I/%L. Python password is generated hex or read from a private trusted file. No lower-trust unvalidated SQL fragment is supplied.

original_title: Mutation audit details accept an unvalidated 'reason' of any JSON type on non-close actions
explanation: Current F08 requires an enabled action capability, correct council/context, valid version, CSRF and idempotency key. Non-close actions still accept an object-valued reason; audit persists it and CommandMAPS renders details.reason as a React child. Scope and entitlement checks narrow the actor but do not validate the stored type. This is a stored reader-availability path, not demonstrated XSS.

original_title: Errors from workers are swallowed with no logging
explanation: Routing and provisioning deliberately discard raw provider exceptions but persist generic failure/event state. Top-level provisioning failure logs a generic message. Safe error categories and correlation would improve diagnosis; errors are not wholly silent.

original_title: Malformed stored password hash throws (HTTP 500) instead of failing the login
explanation: verifyPassword assumes a valid stored salt:hex digest; wrong-length Buffer causes timingSafeEqual to throw. Corrupt database state can turn that login into 500. Shipped hash writers generate valid lengths; ordinary callers cannot supply stored hashes.

original_title: UI shows <slug>-commandmaps hostname that can differ from the real municipalityToken hostname
explanation: Wizard constructs slug-commandmaps, while municipalityToken substitutes aliases/UUID tokens for reserved or long slugs. The displayed promise can differ from authoritative naming. Actual routing still uses its manifest.

original_title: Platform header avatar initials are hard-coded to the seeded operator
explanation: Header initials remain the literal SI although operator name is dynamic. Cosmetic identity display issue, not an authentication substitution.

original_title: API helpers assume every response is JSON
explanation: Both API clients call response.json before testing status. HTML proxy failures produce parse errors rather than a useful HTTP error. Existing API normally emits JSON; injected script or authentication bypass is not implied.

original_title: Job refresh reports success when there is no job; session expiry on first load is not handled
explanation: CommandMAPS initial queue load only sets an error on 401 after session retrieval, leaving stale signed-in state. Platform action-without-job branch exists but normal buttons require a present job; universal false success is not demonstrated.

original_title: Date/time formatting is inconsistent: some views use browser time zone, others Australia/Melbourne
explanation: Routing/provisioning timestamps use browser local time; other shared formatters use Australia/Melbourne. Users in another time zone see inconsistent presentation. Freshness calculation uses epoch milliseconds and is unaffected.

original_title: Route bootstrap script resets municipality status on every run and uses a positional INSERT
explanation: Bootstrap status reset now preserves Suspended and Activated/Disabled admins. Existing-runtime release explicitly skips reseeding/bootstrap. A positional resource-context INSERT remains brittle against future schema changes, not a present release data-loss path.

original_title: Provisioning capacity cap counts failed jobs; registration maps every unique violation to 'slug or email in use'
explanation: Failed jobs count toward the two-resource budget because failed effects can retain real resources; simply ignoring them or deleting jobs would weaken the cost/ownership guard. Blanket 23505 messaging is real but no reachable unrelated constraint collision was established.

original_title: First-admin temporary password is shown once and cannot be recovered if the response is lost
explanation: The old temporary-password workflow is superseded by F07 activation and reissue. F08 additionally corrected the wizard copy to describe a one-time activation link; registration does not deliver a usable password. Existing pending hashes are not activation credentials.

original_title: Zone assignment uses the arithmetic mean of polygon vertices, not a centroid or intersection
explanation: centroidOfPolygon averages all vertices, including ring and hole vertices, then assigns by that point. This is not an area centroid or overlap rule and can misclassify geometries; frequency in existing data is unknown.

original_title: Geo scripts have no fetch timeout, swallow malformed rows silently and rely on fragile heuristics
explanation: JS fetch lacks an explicit deadline and Python drops malformed JSONL rows without a count. Python HTTP calls do specify timeouts, including 300 seconds for streaming. Geometric heuristics and URL validity require representative source-data validation.

original_title: CI runs only npm run check and two browser suites; infrastructure guards, cloud/ingress tests, Python and audit are never run
explanation: CI now runs actual Caddy authority/login suites and three browser suites. Cloud acceptance, cfn-guard, Python lint and npm audit remain outside this workflow. Requiring disruptive cloud tests on each PR would need a dedicated safe environment.

original_title: Security group / template inconsistencies in the CloudFormation stacks
explanation: Hard-coded 172.31/16 egress reduces F05 VPC portability; plain-string IDs reduce early validation and backup retention is one day. These do not expose the database publicly: ingress is security-group restricted and data is synthetic. Failure is not inevitable in every other VPC.

original_title: Documentation and package scripts reference files that do not exist
explanation: Scaffold scripts reference missing stub-task.mjs; .env.example carries obsolete configuration/validator references. Root documented build explicitly excludes those scaffolds. They should not be represented as functioning packages.

original_title: Third-party scripts in wireframe pages have no Subresource Integrity (4 of 28 external script tags)
explanation: Print replicas contain external scripts without integrity attributes, but shipped ingress serves built apps, not _ds wireframes. Treat as a preview-page dependency concern, not a demonstrated deployed-app code execution path.

original_title: ESLint and Prettier do not cover domains/, geo-data/ or Python; two first-party files already fail Prettier
explanation: Active lifecycle.mjs is imported by API but excluded from explicit lint/format scope; GIS/Python are excluded too. Exact old formatter/ruff failure counts were not rerun and must not be presented as current results.

original_title: Placeholder directory typo and empty packages inflate the structure
explanation: Partly resolved on current main: apps/civicmaps-platform/stc/.gitkeep was deleted in c011cc7. Other explicitly labelled scaffold packages remain. Do not recreate or report the removed directory as a current defect.

original_title: Two web apps duplicate tsconfig, tooling and dependency declarations with no workspace or shared base
explanation: The two app tsconfigs duplicate configuration and the root has no npm workspaces. Root and CommandMAPS manifests overlap dependency declarations; the Platform manifest currently relies on root dependencies. Current declarations do not establish actual version drift or failed installation. Broadly saying both apps duplicate dependency declarations is inaccurate.

original_title: Invalid HTML and a misnamed generic component
explanation: Queue button contains a div contrary to phrasing-content rules. Confirm hard-codes Turn off pack, but its actual caller is pack removal, so that label is correct today. Accessibility impact requires browser/assistive-technology assessment.

original_title: geo-data package manifest points at a missing entry point and uses a different scope
explanation: Private geo package declares absent index.ts as main/types. Current GIS usage invokes scripts directly; no root consumer imports this package. @maps naming is inconsistent but not equivalent to the expressly discouraged cmaps abbreviation.

original_title: Python dependencies are undeclared and generated outputs are committed
explanation: Python imports third-party dependencies with no requirements/pyproject lock manifest found. Committing generated data alone is not wrong; provenance and reproducible dependency versions matter more than file size.

original_title: createApp() is a 309-line function holding every council route
explanation: createApp still owns many routes. Complexity warrants focused refactoring only when behaviour can be preserved; function length is not proof of an authorisation defect.

original_title: Other duplication: route list SQL, API client, side-of-street logic and municipality token rules
explanation: API clients, route SQL and side calculations repeat; token rules occur in JS and a versioned migration. Migration duplication can deliberately preserve historical upgrade semantics. No actual JS/SQL mismatch was established by this claim.

original_title: Test hooks and fixture identities live in production modules
explanation: Worker fault environment variable is restricted to NODE_ENV=test. failVersion is a trusted JS API argument and is not populated by HTTP callers. Exact synthetic municipality aliases preserve shipped identities. No untrusted fault-injection path exists in the supplied trace.

original_title: Large single functions in routing middleware and data-resources
explanation: Routing and resource functions contain substantial control flow, but line count supplies no source-to-sink failure. Refactor opportunistically after behavioural coverage, not as an urgent security repair.

original_title: Infrastructure identifiers (AWS account ID, RDS endpoint, secret ARN) committed in source
explanation: Project identifiers, endpoints and ARN references are configuration metadata, not credentials. IAM still controls access and documentation explicitly says the runtime cannot read the master secret. Portability is a separate concern.

original_title: Resources carry ReviewAfter=2026-10-21 (four days from the assessment date)
explanation: ReviewAfter is a review tag, not an automatic expiry or deletion policy. Date is 21 October 2026, three days after this review. Resources and populated data must not be removed merely because the date arrives.

original_title: npm override replaces rollup with the WebAssembly build for all consumers
explanation: WASM Rollup override is documented for the filesystem/tooling constraints and lockfile-managed. Non-default implementation alone is not misconfiguration; no measured regression or compromised dependency was supplied.

original_title: Vite dev server may read the whole repository
explanation: Vite allow-list includes repository root, but documented commands bind to loopback and deployed runtime serves built apps. No supported untrusted network exposure was supplied; narrow allow-list if practical without breaking fonts.

original_title: Design-system wireframe viewer is duplicated byte-for-byte and evaluates strings with new Function
explanation: The two support.js files have identical SHA256 and evaluate code, but are design-preview tooling outside shipped built-app roots. No production unsafe-eval requirement or untrusted source was established.

original_title: Dead code and duplicated effect
explanation: Unused Python helpers/constants and repeated directory-loading logic remain. Imperative load is called after mutations; the effect serves initial load and cancellation, so it is not simply a redundant effect to remove.

original_title: Health and status payloads hard-code 'local-synthetic' mode in every environment
explanation: Health now reports ingress/local separately from synthetic data. Platform municipality response still says local-synthetic. Public DB readiness query is intentional; no workload-based denial of service is established by its presence.

original_title: Authenticated reads take row locks on every request
explanation: FOR SHARE locks ensure revocation serialises with authorised work; shared readers do not inherently exclude each other. Missing expiry/user indexes are optimisation candidates. Removing locks without replacement would weaken revocation guarantees; load regression is unmeasured.

original_title: Platform UI polls detail every 2 s with no back-off while jobs or routes are pending
explanation: Pending work still polls every two seconds, but failures back off to fifteen seconds, settled views poll at fifteen seconds, requests time out and only one effect owns reads. No overlapping unbounded polling loop remains; healthy stuck jobs still warrant capacity measurement.

original_title: Routing worker sleeps without honouring SIGTERM
explanation: SIGTERM changes a flag but does not cancel the active probe or ten-second timer, so graceful exit can be delayed. This is bounded latency, not failure to handle SIGTERM at all; no actual service-manager shutdown failure is established.
